takeaways.label: Record quarter, broad-based growth
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 48% YoY with every vertical delivering strong double-digit growth, driven by structural GPU migration, premium mobility, and higher ASPs across PCs and smartphones.

takeaways.label: TSG is the standout, powered by a structural shift
takeaways.text: Revenue jumped 91% YoY, fueled by a CPU-to-GPU transition where ASPs are often 4x; large deals alone exceeded ₹3,800 crores.

takeaways.label: Price-led growth masks volume fragility
takeaways.text: PC and smartphone revenue growth is heavily ASP-driven; consumer PC volumes are declining and premium smartphone growth is expected to "hit a wall."

takeaways.label: Arena losses are a drag, with an uncertain path
takeaways.text: Redington's share of loss was ₹115 crores, including a Turkey exit and impairment; a new management team is in place but turnaround timing is unpredictable.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether post-Diwali demand contraction from price increases materializes, the trajectory of West Asia geopolitical disruption, and any signs of AI capex pullback affecting TSG.

sections.title: The Structural GPU Shift in TSG

points.label: A real transition, not a pricing blip
points.text: Enterprises are migrating from CPUs to GPUs, driving ASPs to roughly 4x in most cases; management frames this as a durable technology cycle, not a short-term phenomenon.

points.label: Large deals dominate the math
points.text: ₹3,800 crores in large deals drove 90% of TSG growth; excluding them, TSG still grew a healthy 35%, showing broad-based underlying demand across servers, storage and networking.

points.label: Capital efficiency on large deals
points.text: Capital investment on the funded portion is almost nil, with only a non-funded portion being utilized for the purpose of large deal, making the return "almost infinite."

points.label: The AI capex risk
points.text: If enterprise AI-related spend incrementally declines, it would directly affect TSG and the data center piece, and to a lesser extent PCs; SSG's cloud and security growth is expected to be more resilient.

quotes.text: Hariharan: "It's not really a pricing phenomenon as a lot of people think. There is a real transition happening from CPUs to GPUs. And this is based on enterprises adopting GPUs and migrating GPUs."

sections.title: Price-Led Growth and the Volume Question

points.label: ASPs are doing the heavy lifting
points.text: Price increases on smartphones and PCs have been 30% to 50% YoY, driving revenue growth even as consumer PC unit volumes decline and Microsoft activation data shows negative 20%, 30%.

points.label: Commercial PCs are holding up better
points.text: Enterprise volumes are between 0% and 5%, 0% and 7%, with AI PC adoption above 40% in the commercial segment versus only 10% among consumers; management has not yet seen minus 10%, minus 20% type demand softening on the commercial side.

points.label: Premium smartphones face a ceiling
points.text: Growth in the premium segment, driven by fold phones, AI features and EMI financing, is expected to decelerate; entry-level and midrange are already seeing a slowdown.

points.label: The elasticity unknown
points.text: Management acknowledges that at some point price increases will slacken actual unit consumption, but cannot separate value-led from price-led growth in the current mix shift toward AI-capable PCs.

quotes.text: Hariharan: "...definitely, we're going to hit a wall somewhere. And truly, the entry level in the midrange of the market is seeing some of those."

sections.title: Arena: Restructuring with an Open-Ended Timeline

points.label: The loss this quarter
points.text: Redington's share of Arena losses was ₹115 crores, comprising a business loss, a Lira business transition loss from rebates and discounts not fully aligned with vendors, and an exceptional ₹40 crores impairment of intangibles.

points.label: What has been done
points.text: A completely new management team is in place, the high-interest-rate working capital business in Turkey has been exited, and the subsidiary is restructuring its portfolio while developing a dollar-denominated growth avenue.

points.label: What cannot be forecast
points.text: Management explicitly cannot estimate turnaround timing, citing "new curve balls" that keep emerging in the Turkey market; the focus is on eliminating negatives and getting to a cleaner business.

quotes.text: Hariharan: "We really cannot estimate all the new curve balls that are coming up in the Turkey market. That's the challenge."

points.label: H2 geography outlook
points.text: India, GGCL and Africa are expected to remain very strong growth drivers; UAE and KSA growth will depend on geopolitical disruption, which is an unknown.

points.label: H2 segment caution
points.text: TSG and SSG are expected to lead; management is more cautious on ESG and MSG because of price-volume elasticity and volume dampening from price increases.

rows: Premium mobility, new product introductions, higher PC ASPs, data center wins, and sustained software/cloud/security expansion.

Teams adapted to logistics disruption, longer collection cycles and tighter liquidity; strong growth in value-led categories, though inventory is on the high side due to supply chain stress from Strait of Hormuz closure.
Healthy momentum across both Apple and Android, driven by premiumization and new product launches.
Highest quarterly revenue to date; higher ASPs the principal driver, with a sequential increase in commercial PC volumes.
All SBUs grew; cybersecurity "sprung back nicely" and cloud remained strong; gross margin above 6% and profitability above Redington's average.

sections.title: AI, Platforms and the Business Model Shift

points.label: AI Exchange moves to commercial activity
points.text: Launched two quarters ago, the platform is now engaging hundreds of partners and ISVs, with a growing funnel; management sees it as a long journey aimed at solving the gap between AI ambition and enterprise disillusionment with execution.

points.label: CloudQuarks 2.0 and lifecycle tools
points.text: Rolled out across Middle East and Africa; TrackMyCloud and Reonix are seeing better partner adoption, supporting the ecosystem orchestration play.

points.label: Neo cloud data center opportunity
points.text: Management sees a ₹150,000 crore opportunity over the next four years, where distribution plays a role in hardware deal sourcing, ecosystem orchestration, filling capacity, and professional services; margins are lower than normal business unit run-rates but ROCE targets are maintained and leverage is good because incremental opex is minimal.

points.label: The 3–5 year margin ambition
points.text: Through ecosystem orchestration, CloudQuarks, marketplace, automation tools and lifecycle management, management expects to improve gross margins on the combined SSG and TSG business over time.

quotes.text: Hariharan: "Increasingly, people are getting a little bit disenchanted and disappointed in terms of getting that to happen. So an AI exchange type of a platform was to solve that gap..."

sections.title: Balance Sheet, Opex and Working Capital

points.label: Opex run-rate reset
points.text: Opex rose sharply due to higher AR provisioning in Arena and India, investments in SSG, and Middle East insurance costs from the war situation; sustainable steady-state opex is now expected to track between ₹950 crore and ₹1,000 crore per quarter.

points.label: Working capital
points.text: Days are being controlled at the lower end of the 35–40 day range, but the quantum of working capital and debt is expected to rise with growth; free cash flow was negative ₹1,871 crore in Q2, attributed to higher growth in a working-capital-intensive business.

points.label: Debt comfort
points.text: Debt-to-equity is at 0.5–0.6x, well below the global distribution norm of 0.6–0.8x; management is comfortable and will return to the market for additional capital when required.

points.label: Inventory is not the concern
points.text: Management is not worried about inventory when prices are rising; the concern is on receivables, particularly in Turkey where general liquidity conditions are tight.

quotes.text: Krishnan: "...when we see the requirement for additional capital times, we will come back to the market at the right time."

items.title: India data center large deals
items.text: Q2 FY27 large deals exceeded ₹3,800 cr (about 9% of group revenue), up from ~₹2,500 cr in all of FY26, with a good chunk from India data centers that are almost all NeoCloud. Management sizes India's data center opportunity at ₹150,000 crore over the next four years as capacity scales from 1.5 GW toward 12 GW, and the deals carry a maintained ROCE with almost nil capital on the funded portion.

items.title: AI PC and GPU migration
items.text: CPU-to-GPU migration is lifting server ASPs almost 4x, and endpoint revenue grew 38% in Q2 FY27 to a record on 30-50% PC price increases, with AI PCs already over 40% of commercial PC penetration. Management sees no tapering of the AI hardware business for the next 4-6 quarters and OEMs indicate supply will stay tight for 12-18 months, extending the price benefit through FY27.

items.title: SSG cloud and software scale-up
items.text: SSG grew 39% in Q2 FY27 with cloud up 67% in Q1 FY27, and gross margin above 6% versus the company's ~2% operating margin, backed by 130+ brands and 10,000+ partners. Management targets a 20% software share of business, and only 7-8% of cloud business currently flows through distribution, leaving most of the shift to managed subscriptions still ahead.

items.title: Premium mobility and DTR in India
items.text: Mobility grew 40% in Q2 FY27 to 34% of group revenue on premiumization, with India's premium segment growing 8x while the overall market grew 1%, and all three brands Redington distributes sitting in the premium category. The direct-to-retail model for one premium Android brand lifted its revenue share from 1.3% to 10.2% over five years across ~6,000 outlets, and iPhone 18 base-model launch plus new iPad and laptop SKUs could make Q4 stronger than the usual Q2-Q3 seasonal peak.

items.title: AWS AI distribution in META
items.text: On 22 Oct 2026 Redington Gulf signed a strategic collaboration agreement with AWS to accelerate AI adoption across Middle East, Turkey and Africa, with focus on agentic AI in Saudi Arabia and expansion via AWS Marketplace. Combined with Microsoft's Frontier Distributor designation (Jul 2026) and an AI go-to-market team being built in India and Middle East, this gives signed vendor backing to monetise AI beyond hardware.

items.title: AI Exchange marketplace
items.text: Launched mid-March 2026, AI Exchange now carries 250+ productized AI agents from ISVs and is generating revenue and go-to-market momentum, described as "somewhat like what cloud was 10 years back". A new revenue stream with no equivalent in traditional distribution - professional services already almost doubled in Q1 FY27 as this attaches to deals.

items.title: ASEAN and new geography expansion
items.text: Southeast Asia was formally established as a cluster in FY26 with Malaysia as the first step and planned entries into Indonesia and Thailand in FY27, targeting cloud, everything-as-a-service and professional services. With South Africa, CIS and Turkey already entered, the geographic runway supports the ambition to climb from the number-seven global position.

items.title: Arena Turkey loss elimination
items.text: Arena has exited the lira business and BDF contract, cutting debt from $120-130 mn to $90 mn and all-in finance cost from ₹69 cr to ₹37 cr, with the business right-sized to ~$0.5 bn of largely USD-denominated IT and cloud revenue. Losses are expected to continue at a reduced level this year with a real profitability turnaround the following year - a swing from the ₹115 cr Q2 FY27 hit to Redington's share.

items.title: Renewable energy vertical
items.text: Solar/renewables revenue reached ₹111 cr in Q2 FY27, up 541% YoY globally and 578% in SISA, on B2B rooftop models with 100 MW of solar capacity already created in India. India's installed solar base is projected to grow at ~19% CAGR to 2031 against a 500 GW national target, giving the young vertical a fast-expanding addressable market.
